solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Enthusiastic amateur possibly entitled to employ volunteers

indicators.note: to employ is to take on, so the shuffled letters hold the volunteers inside them
possibly signals that the letters of entitled could be arranged some other way

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: A keen hobbyist, perhaps feeling entitled, takes on unpaid helpers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Enthusiastic amateur' is a single definition; 'possibly' scrambles the fodder and 'to employ' wraps it round the Territorial Army letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A dabbler who pursues an art or interest for pleasure rather than profession is an enthusiastic amateur.

clue.text: Some desperate ideas turned up in Parliament

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means read from bottom to top
some means only part of the following words is used

explanation.surface: A few frantic proposals surfaced in the legislature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes TEID from 'desperate ideas'; 'turned up' reads it upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A legislative assembly in some countries, such as Japan's, bears this name.

clue.text: Beware guard

definitions.meaning: a warning to be careful, as in the imperative 'watch it!'

explanation.surface: Watch out for the sentry.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation warns people to beware; the noun is a person on watch.

clue.text: Very high-scoring draw? Perfect!

definitions.meaning: a tie in which each side scores twenty
the normal standard of sharp eyesight

explanation.surface: A cracking tied game: just ideal!
explanation.walkthrough: A 20-20 score is a high draw in football; perfect vision is described with the same figures.
explanation.definitionFit: Normal sharp eyesight is described as twenty over twenty, so the phrase means perfect.

clue.text: Worker, perhaps, left deer playing like stags

parts.note: a worker ant is one kind of ant

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters frolicking into a new order

explanation.surface: An insect left the deer frolicking like stags.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges DEER into RED.
explanation.definitionFit: Male deer carry branched horns, so being horned in that way is like stags.

clue.text: Attempt to secure one pound for hat

indicators.note: securing means holding fast, so the attempt wraps around the other letters

parts.note: a try is an attempt
I is the Roman numeral for one
LB is the abbreviation for a pound in weight, from libra

explanation.surface: Try to bag a hat for a pound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pound' here is the weight abbreviation, not money; 'to secure' signals wrapping.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft felt headpiece with a dented crown is a type of hat.

clue.text: Benefactor in need of new access

indicators.note: being in need of something means lacking it, so the letter for new is missing

parts.note: a donor is someone who gives money, a benefactor

explanation.surface: A generous patron needs fresh ways in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in need of' takes N out of DONOR.
explanation.definitionFit: An entrance you pass through, such as a hinged panel in a wall, gives access to a room.

clue.text: Intimidate on account of a heartless wife

parts.note: over can mean because of, as in a row over money

indicators.note: heartless removes the middle letters of wife, keeping its ends

explanation.surface: Bully someone over a callous spouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' leaves WE from 'wife'.
explanation.definitionFit: To fill someone with awe so they are subdued is to intimidate them.

clue.text: Salesman with ordinary tale about independent store

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the tale goes round the letter

parts.note: a story is a tale

explanation.surface: A sales agent tells a plain story about an independent shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts I inside STORY after its S.
explanation.definitionFit: A place where things are kept, a depository, is a store.

clue.text: Selfish guest finally interrupts flustered concierge

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into, so the letter goes into the middle of the jumbled letters
someone flustered is in a state of disorder, so these letters are jumbled
finally points to the closing letter of the word guest

explanation.surface: A self-centred hotel guest barges in on a harassed porter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flustered' is the anagram signal for the porter's title; 'interrupts' puts the guest's last letter into the scramble.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-centred people think only of their own interests, which is being selfish.

clue.text: Retain part of castle

definitions.meaning: the central fortified tower of a medieval castle

explanation.surface: Keep possession of a section of a fortress.
explanation.definitionFit: Holding on to something is retaining it; the strongest inner tower of a castle has the same name.

clue.text: Privateers arranged voyage on vacation — it prolongs life

indicators.note: arranged means put in a new order
on vacation means emptied, so only the ends of voyage are kept

explanation.surface: Pirates planned a voyage on holiday, something that keeps them going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' turns PRIVATEERS into PRESERVATI; 'on vacation' leaves VE from 'voyage'.
explanation.definitionFit: A chemical added to food to stop it spoiling extends its shelf life.

clue.text: Son enters fashionable crowd

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so this letter sits within the word for fashionable

parts.note: something hot is currently in fashion
S is the abbreviation for son in genealogies

explanation.surface: A young man joins a trendy set of people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enters' puts S inside HOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A large number of people or things, as in 'a whole host of problems', is a crowd.

clue.text: Shame lawyers stopping terrible smears

indicators.note: stopping means plugging a gap, so the lawyers go into the middle of the jumbled letters
terrible suggests the letters are in a dreadful mess

parts.note: the Bar is the collective term for barristers

explanation.surface: Barristers halt a campaign of nasty slurs, to someone's disgrace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shame' is a verb here; 'terrible' scrambles the slurs and 'stopping' plugs the barristers into them.
explanation.definitionFit: To shame someone is to make them feel awkward and humiliated, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Shocking cargo regularly carried by strange old American

indicators.note: carried by means held inside, so the picked letters sit within the word for strange

parts.note: outré means bizarre or strange

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of cargo

explanation.surface: A bizarre old Yank is carrying freight in a shocking way.
explanation.walkthrough: Outré is a French borrowing for bizarre; 'regularly' picks even letters of the freight word and 'carried by' tucks them in.
explanation.definitionFit: Something scandalous that offends decency is shocking.

clue.text: Nameless, like common people?

definitions.meaning: having no name or heading, as an artwork with no title
commoners hold no aristocratic title such as lord or duke

explanation.surface: An anonymous person, just like ordinary folk.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful second sense: commoners lack a noble title.
explanation.definitionFit: A work given no name has no title; commoners likewise carry no rank of nobility.

clue.text: Approval in note to seize property? Quite the opposite

indicators.note: seizing means grabbing hold of, which suggests one piece wrapped round another
this reverses the roles just given, so the property takes hold of the note

parts.note: an asset is a piece of property or something owned

explanation.surface: Permission is sought in a letter to confiscate someone's belongings.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, N would seize ASSET; 'Quite the opposite' flips it so ASSET holds N.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving agreement or consent to a proposal is giving approval.

clue.text: Understand right to support Conservatives

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means sitting below, so this word follows

parts.note: Cons is short for Conservatives
true means correct or right

explanation.surface: Grasp that it is correct to back the Tories.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to support' places TRUE beneath CONS in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: To interpret a meaning is to understand it.

clue.text: Bat's loud noise

definitions.meaning: a strung bat used in tennis or squash

explanation.surface: A flying mammal is making a din.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bat' suggests the animal, but it is the sporting implement for tennis.
explanation.definitionFit: The strung frame used to hit a tennis ball is a bat of sorts; a din is also called this.

clue.text: What wags cut short?

definitions.meaning: a dog's appendage that wags, read as a mongrel's tail

explanation.surface: Who trims back the jokers?
explanation.walkthrough: 'wags' looks like jokers; split the answer and it is a mongrel's tail.
explanation.definitionFit: To reduce or abridge something is to cut it short; split in two, it names what a dog wags.

clue.text: Woo current Queen — and her attendant

parts.note: to court is to woo
I is the symbol for electric current in physics
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A suitor chases a modern queen and the lady who waits on her.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of a royal household who attends the monarch is one of her attendants at court.

clue.text: Repeat line from intellectual

indicators.note: from here means taken away from, so this letter is removed

parts.note: literate can mean well-read or intellectual

explanation.surface: Echo a sentence from a scholar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' takes L away from LITERATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To say or do again is to repeat, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Protect two small businesses, overdrawn, to be gutted

indicators.note: two means the abbreviation appears twice

parts.note: Co is short for company, a business

indicators.note: gutted means the insides are removed, leaving the ends of overdrawn

explanation.surface: Shield a couple of little firms that are in the red from collapse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be gutted' leaves ON from 'overdrawn'.
explanation.definitionFit: To wrap something up snugly to shelter it, like a silkworm's casing, is to protect it.

clue.text: Signatory's funny turns

indicators.note: funny means odd or peculiar, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The person signing a contract has comic twists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'funny' rearranges SIGNATORY.
explanation.definitionFit: Circular spinning movements around a centre are turns or rotations.

clue.text: Some refuse last round to get drinks

indicators.note: turning round means the letters run back to front
some means only part of the following words is used

explanation.surface: Some people turn down the final round at the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes SELA from 'refuse last'; 'round' turns it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Pints of beer are drinks; the word is a plural noun for these brews.

clue.text: Study time in depression

parts.note: a den is a small private study room

explanation.surface: Revising for a long time leads to feeling low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'depression' means a hollow, not low mood.
explanation.definitionFit: A hollow mark in a surface is a depression.

clue.text: Scottish port's over prohibition

parts.note: O is the cricket scorebook abbreviation for an over
a ban is a prohibition

explanation.surface: A Highland harbour town has ended its ban.
explanation.definitionFit: A town and ferry port on the west coast of Scotland, famed for its whisky distillery.

clue.text: Organise slapdash decoration

indicators.note: slapdash means carelessly done, so the letters are thrown together anew

explanation.surface: Arrange some sloppy ornamentation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slapdash' rearranges DECORATION.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring elements into working harmony is to organise them.

clue.text: Only fish

explanation.surface: Nothing but fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A single, exclusive thing is the only one; a flatfish shares the name.

clue.text: Prior wished to have no limits on grant and books

indicators.note: with no limits means the outer letters are taken off

parts.note: wanted means wished for
to cede is to grant or yield
NT is the New Testament, a collection of books

explanation.surface: A monastic head wanted no restrictions on funding and literature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to have no limits' strips W and D from WANTED, leaving ANTE; 'Prior' is the definition, not a monk.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that comes before another in time or order is earlier, the adjective sense of prior.
